planting.note: Root leaf or stem cuttings, or plant offsets, in spring in gritty, well-drained cactus-and-succulent mix in full sun; strong light brings out both the deepest leaf color and the most pronounced tip horns.

directions: This agavoides selection forms a tight, symmetrical rosette of thick, triangular leaves that taper to an elongated point, each tip bearing a pair of small, raised, horn-like projections that give the cultivar its name and set it apart from smoother-tipped agavoides forms. Leaf color ranges from bronze-green in shade to a deep reddish-purple across the whole leaf in strong sun and cool weather. Grow in sharply drained soil in full sun, watering deeply and then letting the mix dry out completely before watering again, and propagate from offsets or individual leaf and stem cuttings.

planting.note: Plant offsets or root individual leaves in spring in gritty, well-drained cactus mix in full sun; cooler temperatures and bright light intensify the reddish tip color.

directions: A broader-leaved agavoides form than selections like 'Red Edge' or 'Lipstick', Corderoyi forms a dense rosette of thick, rounded-triangular leaves in a soft grey-green that deepens to reddish-brown along the tips and margins under strong light. The chunky, slow-growing habit and heavier farinose-grey cast distinguish it from the greener, glossier agavoides cultivars already common in cultivation. Water thoroughly and allow the soil to dry out completely between waterings, and propagate from offsets or leaf cuttings rather than seed to keep the form true.

planting.note: Root offsets or leaf cuttings in spring in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix in full sun to bright light; cool nights deepen the purple-brown coloring.

directions: Like other shaviana selections, Truffles forms a flattened rosette of thin, wavy, deeply ruffled leaves, but in a much darker chocolate-purple to plum tone overlaid with a fine powdery bloom, contrasting with the pale pink-frosted color of the 'Pink Frills' selection already in cultivation. The ruffling becomes more pronounced as the rosette matures and intensifies with bright light and cooler temperatures. Grow in very well-drained, gritty soil, watering deeply and then letting the mix dry fully before the next watering, and keep water out of the crown of the rosette to avoid rot.

planting.note: Root stem or leaf cuttings in spring in lean, gritty succulent mix in full sun; let cut surfaces callus for a few days before setting them on the soil.

directions: This Pachyphytum-Echeveria hybrid carries thick, club-shaped (clavate) leaves, somewhat incurved and coated in a chalky pale blue-grey bloom, loosely arranged into open rosettes on short, lax stems. The powdery leaf surface bruises easily with handling, so it is best displayed where it will not be brushed against. Grow in full sun in sharply drained, gritty mix, watering deeply and then allowing the soil to dry out completely before watering again, and propagate from stem or leaf cuttings since the hybrid does not come true from seed.
